title: Delegate train execution from InterlockingRunner to TrainRunner; never execute wagons in interlocking code

facts.note: Needs an observer that classifies any module (anywhere in the Bun app) as InterlockingRunner-defining, vs. the TrainRunner module, which is exempt. The detector currently only scans src/trains/** (detector scope, see verifier_detail[0]); that path is not a prerequisite of the obligation.

Any change to an InterlockingRunner-defining module, including module-level imports outside the action-handling method; diff-level facts currently surfaced only by the interlocking_delegates.mjs detector findings.

fires: Adding or editing any InterlockingRunner-defining module in a Bun application, wherever it lives
An InterlockingRunner-defining module gains an import of a src/<wagon>/wagon.ts module, anywhere in the module
Interlocking code calls runTrain(...) or iterates `for (... of <expr>.sequence)` to run steps
doesNotFire: Editing the production TrainRunner module, including its own step loop
Changes to wagon modules or other code that never defines an InterlockingRunner
A tree with no InterlockingRunner at all (covered by coder.bun.interlocking-runner-exists)

given: A Bun application module defines an InterlockingRunner
when: you add or change anything in that module (imports, action handling, train execution)
then: Resolve one admissible train and delegate its execution to `TrainRunner.execute(selectedTrainId, ...)`; the InterlockingRunner must never execute wagons itself.
avoid: Importing a `src/<wagon>/wagon.ts` module anywhere in the InterlockingRunner module
Looping over `<expr>.sequence` (e.g. `train.sequence`) as a step executor
Otherwise invoking wagon steps, choosing the next step inside a train, or bypassing TrainRunner
Suppressing a new direct-execution finding: the rule is strict, not suppressible, and fails CI
unless: The production `TrainRunner` module is the legitimate wagon-step executor; its own step loop is exempt
why: Interlocking is route control, not execution: TrainRunner is the single component that runs wagons and carries Cargo between them; a second executor would compete with it.
evidence: The interlocking_delegates detector reports no direct_wagon_execution finding in any InterlockingRunner-defining module
The InterlockingRunner's execute path returns the result of TrainRunner.execute(selectedTrainId, ...) for the resolved train
verifier_detail: Detector scope: the JS realization scans each InterlockingRunner-defining module under `src/trains/**`; the TrainRunner module is not scanned/flagged (its own step loop is legitimate). Which module is scanned and how patterns are recognized is the per-stack detector's concern.
Flag: (a) direct import of a `src/<wagon>/wagon.ts` wagon module, (b) a `runTrain(...)` call, (c) a `for (... of <expr>.sequence)` executor loop.
Term direct_wagon_execution: an InterlockingRunner module importing a wagon module, calling `runTrain(...)`, or looping over `<expr>.sequence` as a step executor — competing with TrainRunner.
Severity 4; disposition strict: a newly introduced direct-execution pattern is not suppressible and fails CI.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0

Bun-stack realization of the agnostic core obligation coder.train.interlocking-delegates-to-trainrunner (core afokapu/atdd#1251), an agnostic 'route-control, not execution' obligation rendered for the Bun application; the JS detector enforcing it is the atdd.workspace.bun implementation.

Normative source: core runtime spec afokapu/atdd#1251 (InterlockingRunner 'must not': execute wagon steps, choose the next train step inside a train, bypass TrainRunner, or duplicate TrainRunner's execution loop).
Source name: InterlockingRunner delegates execution to TrainRunner and never executes wagons itself (Bun)
